newsitem.title: USA: Crestar sets American Natl acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Crestar sets American Natl acquisition.

text.p: Crestar Financial Corp said Monday it agreed to acquire American National Bancorp Inc in a tax-free exchange of cash or Crestar common, which would value each American National share at $20.25.
Crestar said it intends to purchase in the open market any Crestar shares used in the transaction.

American National is the holding company for American National Savings Bank, a Baltimore-based thrift institution with $505 million in assets, deposits of $330 million and 10 branches in the Baltimore metropolitan area.
The acquisition is subject to approval by bank regulators and American National shareholders.
The merger is expected to be completed during the fourth quarter of 1997, Crestar said.

American National has granted Crestar an option to purchase an additional 792,000 American National shares under certain conditions. There are about 3.6 million shares of American National stock outstanding.
Upon completion of the transaction, American National will become part of Crestar's Baltimore-based Maryland Region, which currently includes 35 branches.

The signing of the definitive agreement marks the beginning of an expected five-month transition period during which plans for combining American National branches, employees, customer accounts and computer systems with Crestar's operations will be completed, announced and implemented, Crestar said.

It said some consolidation among American National's 10 branches is likely, although it is expected that more of American National's branches will remain open than will be merged into Crestar's existing locations. Branch and staffing decisions will be made and announced within the first 90 days of the transition period. American National has about 165 employees. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212 859-1610))
